hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.setting: From 'Censure of Craving': the poet to his own hope.
hook.sanskrit: खलालापाः सोढाः कथमपि तदाराधनपरैः निगृह्यान्तर्बाष्पं हसितमपि शून्येन मनसा । कृतो वित्तस्तम्भप्रतिहतधियामञ्जलिरपि त्वमाशे मोघाशे किमपरमतो नर्तयसि माम् ॥
hook.line: I swallowed insults and forced laughter with an empty heart. Hope, how much longer will you make me dance?
hook.translation: I somehow put up with the taunts of the wicked while trying to please them; I held back my tears and laughed with an empty heart; I folded my hands even before people whose minds were numbed by money. Hope, futile hope, how much more will you make me dance?
hook.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna addresses the Kaurava court, asking Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and make peace.
verse.sanskrit: धर्मज्ञेषु सभासत्सु नेह युक्तमसांप्रतम् / यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः / विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्र प्रपद्यते
verse.line: When wrong crushes right while others watch in silence, the silent are wounded too.
verse.translation: Where right is struck down by wrong and truth by falsehood while the assembly looks on, it is the onlookers who are struck down.
verse.why: You can make the best case for peace and still be refused. Speak anyway.

prasang.title: Krishna's peace embassy to the Kauravas
prasang.summary: Krishna travels to Hastinapura to plead for peace between the cousins. Elders, sages and finally Gandhari urge Duryodhana to share the kingdom; he refuses, even plotting to seize Krishna, and war becomes certain.
prasang.story_hook: Krishna, who could have ended the quarrel by force, chose to walk into his enemies' court with nothing but words.
prasang.lesson: You can make the best case for peace and still be refused. Speak anyway.

verse.for_you: You have given a decade to the house, the car, the title, and the silence around you. The empty feeling is the weight of your own sight. You saw what was done, and the house still holds your witness.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing today that you saw and did not speak about.
verse.scene_line: As you sit in the car, you are the silent one in the assembly, and the silence has already wounded you.

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The creation story: last of all, dharma is made.
verse.sanskrit: स नैव व्यभवत् तच्छ्रेयो रूपमत्यसृजत धर्मम् । तदेतत्क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात् परं नास्त्यथो अबलीयान् बलीयाꣳसमाशꣳसते धर्मेण यथा राज्ञैवम् । यो वै स धर्मः सत्यं वै तत् तस्मात्सत्यं वदन्तमाहुर्धर्मं वदतीति धर्मं वा वदन्तꣳ सत्यं वदतीत्येतद्ध्येवैतदुभयं भवति ॥
verse.line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
verse.translation: Still he did not flourish. So he created a higher form, dharma. Dharma is the power over power; nothing is higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can stand up to a strong one, as with the help of a king. That dharma is truth. So people say of one who speaks truth, 'He speaks dharma,' and of one who speaks dharma, 'He speaks truth.' Both are the same.
verse.why: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

prasang.title: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

why: the weaker party is not without standing
With what is right the weak can face the strong.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: You have given fourteen years to the work, and the title sits on the desk. That effort is real. The emptiness does not cancel it out.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you did today and name its two possible endings.

why: Weariness at unrewarded work is met by naming both possible ends
Failure is one of two normal outcomes, not a judgement

verse.speaker: Nala
verse.setting: The army is stuck at the ocean; Nala reveals he can build a bridge, which he had not mentioned.
verse.sanskrit: समर्थश्चाप्यहं सेतुं कर्तुं वै वरुणालये। तस्मादद्यैव बध्नन्तु सेतुं वानरपुङ्गवाः॥
verse.line: I can build this. Let's start today.
verse.translation: I too am able to build a bridge across the ocean. So let the best of the monkeys start building it this very day.
verse.why: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

prasang.title: Building the bridge
prasang.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
prasang.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
prasang.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

why: owning a skill he had kept quiet about
start today

verse.line: Work as hard as the ambitious do, but for everyone's good, not your own grip on results.
verse.translation: As the unwise act with attachment to their work, Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing to hold the world together.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

story.title: Shesha walks away from a family that lives on envy
story.story_hook: A thousand brothers, all jealous of each other. The eldest left. What he was given to do next holds up the world.
story.summary: Shesha is the eldest of a thousand brothers who spend their days resenting one another and hating their stepbrother Garuda and his mother. He wants no part of it. He leaves home and takes up austerities so severe that his body dries to skin and sinew.
story.lesson: You may leave what is poisoned by envy; let the steadiness you save become something others can stand on.

verse.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
verse.sanskrit: अरणीमग्निकामो वा मथ्नाति दहृयं मम / वाचा दुरुक्तं देवर्षे तन्मां दहति नित्यदा
verse.line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
verse.translation: My heart is churned the way someone wanting fire churns a fire-stick. The harsh words my relatives say keep burning me, day after day.

prasang.story_hook: Krishna, who guided a war, admitted to a sage that he could not keep the peace in his own family.
prasang.lesson: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram has lain on the shore for three days asking the ocean for a way across. No answer comes.
verse.sanskrit: अवलेपः समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यः स्वयम्। प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता॥ असामर्थ्यफला ह्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः।
verse.line: Calm, patience, honesty and kind words: people who don't value them will read them as weakness.
verse.translation: See the ocean's arrogance: he does not even show himself. Calm, forbearance, straightforwardness and gentle speech, these virtues of the good, are taken by the unworthy as signs of weakness.
verse.why: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.
verse.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.

prasang.title: Ram at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang.summary: Ram lies on kusha grass by the shore for three days, asking the ocean for a way. Ignored, he tells Lakshman that patience is being taken for weakness and takes up his bow. The ocean rises, offers a way (Nala's bridge), and Ram releases the arrow elsewhere at its request.
prasang.story_hook: For three days the prince lay on a bed of grass at the edge of the sea, asking politely.
prasang.lesson: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.

why: patience was offered and treated as incapacity
Humble first, firm after (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 21-22)

verse.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
verse.setting: Draupadi quotes old Prahlada answering his grandson: is forgiveness better, or force?
verse.sanskrit: न श्रेयः सततं तेजो न नित्यं श्रेयसी क्षमा / इति तात विजानीहि द्वयमेतदसंशयम्
verse.line: Force isn't always right, and forgiveness isn't always right. Wisdom is knowing which the moment needs.
verse.translation: Force is not always best, and forgiveness is not always best. Know this for certain, my child: both have their place.
verse.why: Anger rarely heals anything; forgiveness has limits. Wisdom is knowing which a moment needs.
verse.misuse: Forgiveness never means accepting ongoing harm; this verse itself says it has limits.

prasang.title: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
prasang.summary: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
prasang.story_hook: Thirteen years into exile, Draupadi looked at her husband and asked why he was not angry.
prasang.lesson: Anger rarely heals anything; forgiveness has limits. Wisdom is knowing which a moment needs.

verse.for_you: You have given a decade to a life that leaves you hollow. The house and the title are not the answer. Wisdom is knowing which the moment needs. Let that be your shield today.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you choose your response instead of reacting.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet of a house that is full, feeling small while someone else holds the power.

plan_v3.path: mbh.3.28.6 [whose smallness it is: curated list for the wronged stance]
why: Not always force, not always forgiveness: the question of how to respond is a real one.

verse.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verse.setting: The refrain closing each of Uddalaka's lessons.
verse.sanskrit: स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
verse.line: That subtle essence is the self of all that is. That is truth. You are that, Shvetaketu.
verse.translation: That which is the subtle essence: this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu. 'Teach me more, sir.' 'So be it, dear one.'
verse.why: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

prasang.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
prasang.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
prasang.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

why: an empty person is told they are made of the one thing that is real
What you are is not small.

verse.speaker: Sanatkumara
verse.sanskrit: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verse.line: Happiness is in the vast. There is no happiness in the small.
verse.translation: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
verse.why: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

prasang.title: Narada: learned but sad
prasang.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasang.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.
prasang.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when the wanting feels small.
verse.scene_line: You are the one who has mastered the small, yet you stand before the teacher of the vast.

why: the small always leaves a thirst for more; the wanting is for the vast
We act only when we find joy; find where the joy is.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verse.line: If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.
verse.translation: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on doing work for my sake. Even by doing actions for me, you will reach perfection.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

matched.label: I'm burned out and running on empty

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

why: work done for his sake

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: A powerful king offers a fortune for the sage's cow, the source of his whole way of life.
verse.sanskrit: नाहं शतसहस्रेण नापि कोटिशतैर्गवाम्॥ राजन् दास्यामि शबलां राशिभी रजतस्य वा। न परित्यागमयं मत्सकाशादरिंदम ॥
verse.line: Not for any price. Some things are not for sale, however powerful the buyer.
verse.translation: Not for a hundred thousand cows, not for a billion, not for heaps of silver, O king, will I give up Shabala. She stays with me.
verse.why: Envy and force cannot take what someone will not give; real power is built inside.

prasang.title: The king who wanted the cow
prasang.summary: King Vishvamitra is feasted by the sage Vasishtha and covets the wish-granting cow that made it possible. Vasishtha refuses every offer; the king takes her by force and is routed, then fails again with divine weapons. Humbled, he resolves to transform himself through inner discipline instead of force.
prasang.story_hook: A king who had everything saw one thing he could not buy, and it undid him.
prasang.lesson: Envy and force cannot take what someone will not give; real power is built inside.

verse.try_today: Notice one thing today that no offer or title can buy.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the door with the key, and the cow stays with the sage.

why: a plain no to someone far more powerful
what sustains his life is not for sale

story.title: Trishanku is refused, cast out, and taken in by one man
story.story_hook: His teacher refused him. His teacher's sons cursed him. His own court left him. One man said: do not be afraid.
story.summary: King Trishanku wants something no one has done, to reach heaven in his own body. His teacher says it cannot be done. He asks the teacher's sons, and they curse him for going around their father. Overnight he is an outcaste; his ministers and his people walk away. He goes alone to the one person who has no reason to help him.
story.lesson: A person who has been turned away by all and comes for refuge is to be received first and judged later.
story.teaser: His teacher refused him. His teacher's sons cursed him. His own court left him. One man said: do not be afraid.
story.for_you: You have given everything to the title and the house. Now you stand at the gate with nothing left to give, and that is enough. Someone will see you first.

why: A person who has been turned away by all and comes for refuge is to be received first and judged later.
